census.summary: Everything needed for a 2021 census theme exists and was verified live. Geometry: StatCan's ArcGIS REST server (geo.statcan.gc.ca, ArcGIS 11.5) serves 2021 Cartographic and Digital boundary files as MapServers with query in geoJSON, outSR=4326, maxAllowableOffset, pagination (maxRecordCount 6000) and reflective CORS; layers DA (12), CSD (9), CT (11), ADA (10), FED-2013-RO (3) carry DAUID/CSDUID/CTUID/ADAUID/FEDUID + DGUID + LANDAREA + PRUID. NS counts: 95 CSD, 1,670 DA, 108 CT (all Halifax CMA; Cape Breton CA has none), 152 ADA, 11 FED. National shapefile zips also exist (DA CBF 197 MB, CSD 156 MB, CT 13 MB, ADA 155 MB). FED 2023 Representation Order is NOT on StatCan's boundary page or geo server; use Elections Canada's FED_CA_2023_EN-SHP.zip (9.4 MB, 343 features, OGL-Canada, no CORS). Values: the Census Profile SDMX REST API works (DF_DA 1.3, DF_CSD 1.3, DF_FED 1.3/2.0), key A5.<DGUID+...>.1.<char+...>.<1|4>, format=csv/jsondata, CORS OK; 88 DAs x 38 characteristics returned in 9 s. Exact characteristic ids verified (1,2,3,4,5,6,7,40,50,51,56,229,379,383,385,1388,1389,1400,1401,1402,1426-1434,2603-2610). Mi'kmaq is not a separate DA-level row (only 'Indigenous languages'). FED 2023-RO dataflow has all characteristics except population/dwelling counts (chars 1-7 empty, '..'). Provincial sources (data.novascotia.ca, GeoNOVA SOC/ECON/BND) have no 2021 DA/CSD/CT product. Suppression: population < 40 -> all characteristics 'x'; income suppressed if private-household population < 250 or households < 40; counts randomly rounded to 5; DA population within 5 of true. Files written: DA polygons (88) + values JSON with nulls/flags, all-NS CSD GeoJSON with 2021/2016 population, and census.md with every URL. Recommended path: live bbox queries to geo.statcan.gc.ca (or pre-cut NS DAs), batched SDMX value fetches cached per DGUID, Elections Canada geometry for 2023 FEDs, ADAs instead of CTs outside Halifax.

representatives.summary: Verified live on 2026-09-12. Open North Represent (represent.opennorth.ca) is the only single API that returns MP+MLA+(HRM/CBRM) council for a point, with name/party/district_name/email/url/photo_url/offices[type,postal,tel,fax]; CORS open; 60 req/min; NO published data licence and NO per-set last_updated. It is stale where it matters: its NS set is bound to the 2019 boundary set (55 districts) so the new 56th district Chéticamp-Margarees-Pleasant Bay (ED_NO 56, released April 9, 2026; MLA Claude Bourgeois, by-election June 23, 2026) is absent; it lists Chris d'Entremont as Conservative while ourcommons.ca shows Liberal caucus from 2025-11-04; MLA postal fields are a scraper artefact. Municipal coverage in NS is HRM and CBRM only. Authoritative sources: ourcommons.ca search XML/CSV (no contact fields; contact only on member HTML pages), nslegislature.ca /members/profiles (56 rows, Drupal, per-profile civic/mailing address, phone, email; Crawl-delay 10, no feed), halifax.ca district pages (email+phone) and the HRM ArcGIS Who_Is_My_Councillor layer (DIST_ID/DISTNAME/COUNCILLOR only, no contact), cbrm.ns.ca district pages (email+phone). No province-wide municipal officials dataset exists on data.novascotia.ca or Municipal Affairs; NSFM regional directory pages give warden/mayor names + websites only. CSAP publishes 13 members with circonscription name, @csap.ca email and phone, but no circonscription polygons exist anywhere found. The province's ArcGIS service nsgiwa BND_ElectoralBoundaries_UT83/4 has the current 56 districts (ED_NO/ED_NAME/Release_Date), licence unstated. Recommended path: a static, dated directory snapshot keyed by district id (FED 2023-RO id, ED_NO, HRM DIST_ID, CBRM district no.), generated by a repo script from the official sources, with checked_date and official-page link on every card; never call Represent from the browser (privacy + staleness + no licence).

provincialPolls.summary:
Elections NS publishes final 2024 poll-by-poll results as one xlsx (55 sheets ED01-ED55; header row 2: Poll, Polling Location, Electors on Final List, Total Votes* incl. rejected+declined, one column per candidate 'First LAST\nParty', Rejected, Declined; footer Total/Turnout/% valid/Elected). Advance (ADV#), RO-CP, WI and out-of-district rows are separate rows with no elector base; mobile care-home polls are separate rows that can span several PD numbers ('038,039 Mobile2'); combined polls appear as '016/017'. Arithmetic is internally consistent and district totals match the province's GIS results layer exactly.

The current provincial PD layer (PD_ED2026_Carto, 1,817 polygons, 56 districts) is the 2020 release for 54 districts (RELEASE_DATE 'September 1, 2020'), so the 2024 poll numbers join cleanly there: Annapolis 37/37 numbers match, polygon electorcount matches 2021 electors within ~10/poll, locations stable 2021-2024. Inverness and the new ED 56 Chéticamp-Margarees-Pleasant Bay were redrawn and renumbered April 9, 2026 (legislation Feb 2026 implementing the 2025 Boundaries Commission); 2026 PD 001 is Port Hawkesbury while 2024 poll 001 was Pleasant Bay (now ED 56 PD 009). Zero genuine matches for Inverness.

Verdict: a 2024-poll-on-current-division map is defensible for the 54 unchanged districts with a caveat that unmapped advance/RO-CP/write-in votes (45% in Annapolis, and they net favoured the loser there) are excluded. For Inverness it is not; the fix is the still-live but unlinked January 2021 PD shapefile (12.5 MB, not downloaded, contents unverified) or district-level fallback. Files: prov_polls_01/34.json, prov_pd_01/34/56.geojson, prov-polls.md with caveat text.

history.summary: All seven general elections (2003–2024) exist as polygon layers with results attributes on the Elections NS service via nsgiwa.novascotia.ca, and every fetch succeeded with no transfer-limit truncation. Feature counts: 52/52/52 (2003–2009, byte-identical geometry), 51/51 (2013, 2017), 55/55 (2021, 2024). PARTY uses exactly four spellings across all years, and the winner always equals the argmax of the *_Votes columns. Province-wide turnout comes from table 0 (65.79, 59.6, 57.9, 58.2, 53.4, 55.1, 44.9). Files for six years, the turnout table, both Profiles tables, history_summary.json and swing_2021_2024.json were written under scratchpad/geo; verification notes are in scratchpad/research/history.md. Recommended path: use the 0.006-offset GeoJSONs as-is (generalisation is honoured server-side; raw layers are 34 MB), join years within a boundary block on ED_NAME (ED_NO is reused across blocks), take vote shares over sum(*_Votes) because the Total field's meaning changes by year, strip MLA whitespace, and treat 2003 minor-party columns as unreliable. Watch three traps: 2013 and 2017 are separate digitisations of the same boundaries (Shape_Area differs up to 9%); the Profiles tables carry a 56th district (Chéticamp-Margarees-Pleasant Bay, by-election June 23, 2026) absent from every results layer; and the Profiles table labels Lunenburg West "Becky Druhan (Liberal)" because she is now Liberal (legislature site: PC 2021–2025, Independent 2025–2026, Liberal 2026) while the 2024 layer correctly records a PC win. Licence text is not present in the REST metadata (copyright "Elections Nova Scotia" only). The scratchpad is shared with other agents; only my own named files were written or removed.

Suppressed DAs hatched. Inspector 'period ruler': one stacked strip of eight bins oldest to newest in ink tints fading toward paper, ticks at 1960/1980/1990/2000/2005/2010/2015/2021, counts inside bins of 15 or more, the 88-DA county distribution as a hairline outline behind; footer line pointing to the parcel's own PVSC year built when the parcel inspector has one.

ranked.geography: DA at county and neighbourhood zoom; CSD wash at province zoom after one DF_CSD pull; not ED.
ranked.why_top: Stock age is the strongest predictor of what a rural buyer will find (wiring, oil tanks, foundations, well and septic era) and where trades are active. Drawable for 85 of 88 DAs now. The ruler keeps the eight rounded bins visible instead of hiding them behind one number.
ranked.caveats: 25% sample rounded to 5, so bins in a 150-dwelling DA legitimately print 0, 5, 10. Occupied dwellings with usual residents only, so seasonal cottages, often the oldest stock, are outside the universe. Eras are unequal in length, so 'pre-1961' is always darkest; legend says 'share of homes', never 'building activity'. Respondent-reported original build, not renovations. A DA share never dates a house; PVSC year built by AAN is the parcel fact and keeps its own provenance. Attribution with the 2022-12-15 release.

censusIdeas.theme_structure:
Rail category: 'People & Housing' with the subtitle 'Census 2021' and a category footer carrying the two StatCan attribution lines (2022-02-09 counts, 2022-12-15 long form) and the licence-gate notice for any Elections NS ED rung. Category-level control, not a layer: 'Show census context in the inspector' (on by default) which adds the Neighbourhood profile section to parcel, town and district cards. Layer rows are washes and are mutually exclusive (radio behaviour within the category), because two choropleths cannot stack on a paper basemap; the mother-tongue symbol row is the one layer allowed over a wash. Every row shows its geography chip (DA / CSD / ED), its data basis chip (100% or 25% sample) and its release date on hover.

Sub-group 'Homes':
  1. Dwellings not occupied by usual residents — chips ED | CSD | DA, 100%
  2. Period of construction — chips DA (CSD at province after pull), 25% sample; row carries an era selector defaulting to '1960 or before'
  3. One-person households — chips DA, 100%; owner/renter appears only as a related row in the card

Sub-group 'People':
  4. Population change 2016 to 2021 — chips CSD only, 100%; legend at neighbourhood zoom states 'not published at DA scale'
  5. Median age — chips DA, 100%
  6. Mother tongue — chips ED | CSD | DA, 100%; sub-radio French / Indigenous languages (Census label), symbols not fills
  7. Commuting on foot, by bicycle or transit — chips DA, 25% sample, with the pandemic reference-week note in the legend

Sub-group 'Reference' (unfilled, stackable):
  8. Census boundaries — DA hairlines at z >= 11, CSD outlines, ADA when a dataflow is confirmed; used by the profile section for the selected-DA outline

Zoom behaviour is uniform: province zoom draws ED (electoral theme on) or CSD; county zoom draws DA where the DA minScale allows and otherwise ADA/CSD; neighbourhood zoom draws DA with hairlines. Suppressed ('x'), not-applicable ('...') and not-comparable (incomplete enumeration) render as three distinct hatch or dot patterns shared across every row, with a single legend key at the category level so 'no data' never reads as the lowest class. Parked rows, shown greyed with a 'values not yet fetched' tag rather than omitted: 'Arrivals since 2016' (mobility and immigration ids unverified) and 'Median household income' (row in the profile card only; no wash).
rejected: Owners and age (13), bivariate 3x3: unreadable at province zoom by its own admission, terciles hide the absolute spread, the tenure axis is 25% sample on 100-200 household denominators so cells flip on rounding, and pairing age with tenure invites the 'market to target' reading the evidence guide forbids; both variables survive as single-hue rows and as card rows.

Year-round and seasonal homes (11) as dot density: dots seeded uniformly inside a DA are a placeholder the concept itself labels as such, dasymetric seeding against building footprints implies that a peach dot is near a real empty house, and the 1-dot-per-5 rule does not stop a viewer reading dots as addresses; merged into rank 2 as a choropleth, keeping its ramp and ED/CSD province wash.

Growing, holding, thinning (12) as proportional circles: the symbol form fights the quiet paper basemap, Halifax's circle swamps the province view, and the rate-in-label/size-by-count split is harder to read than counts in the card; merged into rank 3, keeping polylabel label placement and the 'not comparable' hatch rule for incompletely enumerated reserves.

Eight eras (14) filmstrip flyout: eight 150 px minimaps of the same DA set is rail real estate spent on a comparison the era selector plus the inspector ruler already gives, and unequal era lengths make seven of the eight panels nearly blank; merged into rank 4.

Household Profile (4) as a standalone card and as an income wash: the four-rail card duplicates the Neighbourhood profile section (rank 1), its reference distribution is currently the 88 Annapolis DAs only, and a median-income choropleth is 2020 pandemic-benefit income suppressed in 4 of 88 DAs, which is the layer most likely to be read as a verdict on a place; income stays as a suppression-aware card row with no map fill.

Arrivals Since 2016 (10): parked, not rejected on merit. Neither the mobility nor the immigration characteristic ids are verified and no values are fetched, so nothing honest can be drawn; the on-hand dwellings-built stand-in is 0 in 53 of 85 DAs. Revisit after resolving ids from CL_CHARACTERISTIC and applying the 250-denominator gate.

Quiet Houses (1) and Between Two Censuses (6) and Filling or Emptying (2), The Age of a Place (7) and Households of One (8) are not rejected: they are the surviving forms inside ranks 2, 3, 5 and 6 and their inspector cards fold into rank 1.

contradictions: GeoNOVA copyright: History reports BND_GeneralElectionResults_UT83 copyrightText = 'Elections Nova Scotia'; Provincial-polls reports copyrightText empty on the same service and layer 7. Neither found licence text; one description is wrong.
